candidate.answerReason: From February 7, 1812, to February 7, 2012, there are 200 ordinary year lengths plus 49 leap days. The weekday advances by 200+49=249 days beyond whole weeks, leaving remainder 4. Four days before Tuesday is Friday.

methods.label: Count leap days and complete weeks
methods.explanation:
Dickens was born \(200\) years before \(2012\), on February \(7,1812\). To recover the weekday, count how many days the weekday advances over those \(200\) years.

The leap day in \(1812\) occurs after his birthday and is included in the interval. The leap day in \(2012\) occurs after the anniversary and is excluded. The multiples of \(4\) from \(1812\) through \(2008\) number
\[
\frac{2008-1812}{4}+1=50.
\]
Among these, \(1900\) is not a leap year because it is divisible by \(100\) but not \(400\). The year \(2000\) is a leap year because it is divisible by \(400\). Thus exactly \(49\) leap days occur.

The elapsed time is \(200\cdot365+49\) days. Since \(365=52\cdot7+1\), each ordinary year contributes one day beyond complete weeks. The total weekday advance therefore has the same remainder as
\[
200+49=249=35\cdot7+4.
\]
The anniversary weekday is four days later in the weekly cycle than the birth weekday. Counting four days backward from Tuesday gives Monday, Sunday, Saturday, Friday. Dickens was born on \(\boxed{\text{Friday}}\), choice A.
